```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5)
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(lubridate)
library(janitor)
library(scales)
library(cluster)
library(knitr)
```

## 1. Executive Summary

This report analyzes `541,909` transaction records from the **UCI Online Retail** dataset (December 2010 – December 2011) to uncover revenue trends, product and market concentration, customer purchasing behavior, and actionable customer segments using **RFM analysis** and **K-Means clustering**.

## 2. Data Import & Cleaning

```{r load-clean}
raw_retail <- read_excel("../data/raw/Online Retail.xlsx")

retail_dedup <- raw_retail %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  mutate(
    customer_id = as.character(customer_id),
    quantity    = as.numeric(quantity),
    unit_price  = as.numeric(unit_price)
  ) %>%
  distinct()

retail_sales <- retail_dedup %>%
  filter(!str_starts(invoice_no, "C"), quantity > 0, unit_price > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    sales_value   = quantity * unit_price,
    invoice_day   = as.Date(invoice_date),
    invoice_month = floor_date(invoice_date, unit = "month")
  )

retail_customers <- retail_sales %>%
  filter(!is.na(customer_id))

cleaning_audit <- tibble(
  Stage = c(
    "1. Raw dataset",
    "2. After removing exact duplicates",
    "3. Valid sales (qty > 0, unit_price > 0, non-C)",
    "4. Valid sales with known customer_id (RFM base)"
  ),
  Rows = c(nrow(raw_retail), nrow(retail_dedup), nrow(retail_sales), nrow(retail_customers)),
  Removed = c(
    0,
    nrow(raw_retail) - nrow(retail_dedup),
    nrow(retail_dedup) - nrow(retail_sales),
    nrow(retail_sales) - nrow(retail_customers)
  )
)
kable(cleaning_audit, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

- **Duplicates:** `5,268` exact duplicate rows were removed.
- **Cancellations & Adjustments:** `9,251` `"C"` cancellation rows, negative/zero quantities, and non-positive unit prices (including `2` bad-debt adjustment rows) were excluded from valid sales.
- **Missing `CustomerID`:** Retained in `retail_sales` for aggregate sales EDA; excluded from `retail_customers` for RFM and clustering.

## 3. Exploratory Data Analysis

```{r eda-monthly}
monthly_sales <- retail_sales %>%
  group_by(invoice_month) %>%
  summarise(monthly_revenue = sum(sales_value), n_invoices = n_distinct(invoice_no), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(monthly_sales, aes(x = invoice_month, y = monthly_revenue)) +
  geom_line(color = "#2C3E50", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "#E74C3C", size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_datetime(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b %Y") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(prefix = "£", scale = 1e-3, suffix = "K")) +
  labs(title = "Monthly Gross Revenue (Valid Sales)", x = "Month", y = "Revenue (£K)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

```{r eda-countries}
country_summary <- retail_sales %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  summarise(
    total_revenue     = sum(sales_value),
    n_invoices        = n_distinct(invoice_no),
    n_customers_known = n_distinct(customer_id, na.rm = TRUE),
    revenue_share_pct = round(sum(sales_value) / sum(retail_sales$sales_value) * 100, 2),
    .groups           = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_revenue))

kable(head(country_summary, 10), digits = 2, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## 4. RFM & K-Means Customer Segmentation

```{r rfm-kmeans}
ref_date <- max(retail_customers$invoice_day) + 1

rfm <- retail_customers %>%
  group_by(customer_id) %>%
  summarise(
    recency   = as.numeric(ref_date - max(invoice_day)),
    frequency = n_distinct(invoice_no),
    monetary  = sum(sales_value),
    .groups   = "drop"
  )

rfm_scaled <- rfm %>%
  mutate(r_log = log1p(recency), f_log = log1p(frequency), m_log = log1p(monetary)) %>%
  select(r_log, f_log, m_log) %>%
  scale() %>%
  as_tibble()

set.seed(42)
km_4 <- kmeans(rfm_scaled, centers = 4, nstart = 25)
rfm_clustered <- rfm %>% mutate(cluster = factor(km_4$cluster))

cluster_profile <- rfm_clustered %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(
    n_customers      = n(),
    customer_share   = round(n() / nrow(rfm_clustered) * 100, 1),
    median_recency   = round(median(recency), 1),
    median_frequency = round(median(frequency), 1),
    median_monetary  = round(median(monetary), 1),
    total_revenue    = round(sum(monetary), 0),
    revenue_share    = round(sum(monetary) / sum(rfm_clustered$monetary) * 100, 1),
    .groups          = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(median_monetary))

kable(cluster_profile, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

## 5. Statistical Analysis

```{r stats}
spearman_cor <- round(cor(select(rfm, recency, frequency, monetary), method = "spearman"), 3)
kable(spearman_cor, caption = "Spearman Rank Correlations Among RFM Metrics")

kw_test <- kruskal.test(monetary ~ cluster, data = rfm_clustered)
kw_test
```

## 6. Recommendations & Limitations

- **Protect & reward High-Value Loyalists (`16.8%` of customers, `65.1%` of customer-identified revenue):** Prioritize VIP retention, early seasonal access before the Q4 peak, and dedicated account support.
- **Nurture Mid-Tier Regulars (`26.8%` of customers, `23.6%` of revenue):** Use replenishment reminders and bundle offers to lift purchase frequency.
- **Convert Recent Low-Frequency buyers (`20.2%` of customers):** Trigger second-purchase incentives within 30 days of their initial order.
- **Selective win-back for Inactive / One-Time buyers (`36.2%` of customers, `6.2%` of revenue):** Run low-cost automated re-engagement rather than heavy discounting.
- **Limitations:** Analysis reflects one UK-based retailer over ~12 months (`Dec 2010 – Dec 2011`), excludes returns/cancellations from gross sales, and lacks margin or marketing-campaign response data.
